key_insight: Physics-informed surrogates can be far more reliable for PV hosting-capacity optimization than data-only models, even when their standard test errors look similar.
engineering_relevance: For distribution-planning workflows, decision-level validation and independent certification are essential because a model that predicts well may still choose unsafe or infeasible operating points.
method: Calibrated PV + distribution-network simulator as the high-fidelity reference
Compared data-only vs physics-informed surrogates inside a stochastic multiobjective optimizer
Used decision-gated enrichment and independent 500-scenario certification to verify Pareto candidates
evidence_signal: Held-out errors were nearly identical, but operational validity differed sharply (44.4% vs 93.4%); inference dropped from 286.0 ms to 0.46 ms for a 60-scenario evaluation, and certification verified all 80 screened candidates.
watch_item: Results are feeder-specific, since cross-feeder transfer caused overvoltage and a 62.7% loss increase on the 33-bus system, so any deployment needs topology-aware auditing.
paper_title: Decision-Gated Surrogate-Assisted Stochastic Optimization with Independent High-Fidelity Certification for Photovoltaic Hosting-Capacity Planning
